examples.sql: WITH "s1" AS (SELECT "stock"."Device_ID" AS e, "device"."Software_Platform" AS g, SUM("stock"."Quantity") AS m1 FROM "stock" JOIN "device" ON "device"."Device_ID" = "stock"."Device_ID"  GROUP BY "stock"."Device_ID", "device"."Software_Platform"), "s2" AS (SELECT SUM("s1"."m1") AS v FROM "s1"), "s3" AS (SELECT "s1"."e" AS e, "s1"."g" AS g, "s1"."m1" AS m1, (CAST("s1"."m1" AS REAL) / "s2"."v") AS m2 FROM "s1" JOIN "s2" ON "s2"."v" IS NOT NULL), "s4" AS (SELECT AVG("s3"."m2") AS v FROM "s3"), "s5" AS (SELECT "s3"."e" AS e, "s3"."g" AS g, "s3"."m1" AS m1, "s3"."m2" AS m2, ("s3"."m2" - "s4"."v") AS m3 FROM "s3" JOIN "s4" ON "s4"."v" IS NOT NULL), "s6" AS (SELECT "s5"."g" AS g, SUM("s5"."m1") AS m1, AVG("s5"."m2") AS m2, AVG("s5"."m3") AS m3 FROM "s5" GROUP BY "s5"."g") SELECT SUM("s6"."m1") AS m1, AVG("s6"."m2") AS m2, AVG("s6"."m3") AS m3 FROM "s6"
examples.instruction:
Step 1. Start from each `stock` record; combine it with each `device` record for which Device ID (`device.Device_ID`) equals Device ID (`stock.Device_ID`), one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); group the kept records by Device ID (`stock.Device_ID`) and software platform (`device.Software_Platform`); each group gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) Device ID (`stock.Device_ID`); (2) software platform (`device.Software_Platform`); (3) the sum of units of device in stock (`stock.Quantity`) in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 2. Start from the rows of step 1; all kept records form one group, which gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) the sum of column (3) of step 1 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 3. Start from the rows of step 1; combine it with the rows of step 2 for which it is not true that column (1) of step 2 is missing, one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); for each kept record, return (1) column (1) of step 1; (2) column (2) of step 1; (3) column (3) of step 1; (4) A ÷ B. Here A is column (3) of step 1; B is column (1) of step 2.
Step 4. Start from the rows of step 3; all kept records form one group, which gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) the average of column (4) of step 3 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 5. Start from the rows of step 3; combine it with the rows of step 4 for which it is not true that column (1) of step 4 is missing, one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); for each kept record, return (1) column (1) of step 3; (2) column (2) of step 3; (3) column (3) of step 3; (4) column (4) of step 3; (5) A − B. Here A is column (4) of step 3; B is column (1) of step 4.
Step 6. Start from the rows of step 5; group the kept records by column (2) of step 5; each group gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) column (2) of step 5; (2) the sum of column (3) of step 5 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none); (3) the average of column (4) of step 5 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none); (4) the average of column (5) of step 5 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
Step 7 (the answer). Start from the rows of step 6; all kept records form one group, which gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) the sum of column (2) of step 6 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none); (2) the average of column (3) of step 6 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none); (3) the average of column (4) of step 6 in the group (missing values ignored; missing when there are none).
